_comment: The prompt set the content engine runs through /api/chat/compare.
DECIDABLE prompts (with `options`) are the valuable ones. An open-ended
question produces ten paraphrases of the same answer, which is not content —
it is filler. A question with a forced pick produces a HEADLINE: '7 models,
4 picked Postgres, 3 picked SQLite'. That is the only shareable artifact
MODUS owns that a single-model competitor structurally cannot produce.
Pick questions that a competent engineer could genuinely answer either way.
A question with a correct answer yields consensus, scores 0, and is dropped.
📊 MEASURED 2026-07-27, first real run, 5 models x 6 prompts on prod:
only 2 of 6 split. The four that went 5/0 unanimous (Postgres, refactor,
monorepo, free-allowance) all have a well-known textbook answer, and frontier
models have all read the same textbook. The two that split (strict-immediately
3/2, raise-vs-bootstrap 4/1) were both about SEQUENCING and RISK TOLERANCE,
where the right answer genuinely depends on values the prompt does not supply.
🔑 So the rule is not 'pick a debatable topic'. It is: pick a question whose
answer turns on something the question deliberately withholds. Expect to burn
3 prompts for every 1 that yields content, and budget the rate limit for it.

prompts.question: You are shipping a solo-founder B2B SaaS that will realistically have under 5,000 users for its first two years. Which database should it launch on?
A four-year-old production codebase has no tests, one original author who left, and a feature backlog the team cannot land. Rewrite it or refactor it incrementally?
A solo founder has a working product, $2k MRR growing 15% a month, and 14 months of personal runway. Raise a seed round now, or keep bootstrapping?
An unknown founder launches a $20/mo AI product with no reviews and no users. Should the first message require a credit card, or should there be a free daily allowance first?
A five-engineer team runs a web app, a mobile app, and three shared packages. Monorepo or separate repos?
You are inheriting a 60k-line JavaScript codebase and adding TypeScript. Turn on `strict` immediately and suppress the errors, or migrate file-by-file with strict off?
A $20/mo product wants to add annual billing. Is a 12-months-for-the-price-of-10 discount too generous, or not generous enough to change behaviour?
An agency owner at $30k/mo revenue is the bottleneck on delivery. Hire a full-time employee, or scale with contractors?
For a new Next.js App Router product with heavy interactivity, should most components default to Server Components, or is a mostly-client architecture more honest about the app's needs?
Should an AI code reviewer be allowed to block a pull request from merging, or should it only ever leave advisory comments?
For daily professional work, is it better to master one frontier model deeply, or to route each task to whichever model is strongest at it?
You need a model to answer questions over a 500-page internal handbook that changes monthly. Build RAG, or just stuff it into a long context window?
It is launch day. One feature out of six is visibly janky but not broken. Ship on time with the janky feature visible, or slip the launch two weeks?
A six-person startup has an engineer who is well-liked, works hard, and ships noticeably slower than everyone else after nine months. Let them go now, or invest another quarter in coaching?
You are doubling your price because you underpriced at launch. Do you grandfather every existing customer forever, or migrate them to the new price after 12 months?
A solo technical founder with a live product and modest revenue is offered a co-founder who is genuinely strong at sales and wants 40%. Take it, or stay solo and hire sales later?
A pre-revenue product with zero users has no test suite. Write tests now while the codebase is small, or wait until something has users worth protecting?
You have copy-pasted the same 30-line block twice and are about to do it a third time. Extract the abstraction now, or copy it a third time and wait for the shape to settle?
A solo developer runs a paid product used during business hours. Set up real paging alerts that wake them at 3am, or check dashboards each morning and accept overnight downtime?
Your team ships code that is 80% AI-generated. Should human review get stricter than it was before, or should it get lighter because the model already handles the mechanical mistakes?
A self-taught developer who ships fast with AI assistance cannot explain how a hash map works internally. Should they stop and learn fundamentals, or keep shipping and learn on demand?
A consultant delivers a client report that they directed and edited but a model drafted. Are they obligated to disclose that a model wrote the first draft?
